name: Hyperliquid

key_findings: The Quantum Resistance FAIL cap (79) sits well above the raw 59.97 and never touches the score -- this result is set by category fundamentals, not by any gate.
On-Chain Health (88) is HYPE's strongest category by a wide margin -- roughly $493B Q1 2026 volume and a majority share of global on-chain derivatives open interest.

Privacy & Confidentiality (15) sits in the sub-floor band. Any account's positions, leverage, and exact liquidation price are published by default through an unauthenticated API, which is financially exploitable per-account state rather than ordinary ledger transparency.

Raw 59.97 rounds to 60, landing on the Emerging Institutional floor with a 0.47-point margin. Roughly one point of movement in any weighted category flips the band, and the category scores were set before the boundary was known.
Clears all three AI foundation gates PASS/PASS/PASS yet still lands in Experimental -- a clear demonstration of gates being a floor, not a guarantee.
Privacy & Confidentiality (18) is HYPE's weakest AI category by a wide margin -- every position and order is publicly watchable in real time.
Agent Tooling (75) and KYA (58) are HYPE's clearest AI strengths -- on-chain human-binding approval and trade-only permissions used by an estimated 20-30% pure-AI-agent volume share.

watch_items: Both axes independently converge on 'strong single-vertical engine, structurally immature everywhere else,' rather than on offsetting strengths.
Quantum Resistance sits at Fail on the basis of silence rather than a stated position -- re-check at every reassessment regardless of trigger.
The published TradFi score is 0.47 points above a tier boundary. Any category revision should state its tier consequence explicitly.
